plan_summary: This plan outlines the steps to install and configure Nginx on an Ubuntu 24.04 system, ensuring security updates are applied, dependencies are resolved, and a basic web server configuration is deployed.
assumptions: The Ubuntu 24.04 host has network access to update repositories.
The user has sudo privileges or root access.
A basic HTTP response is expected immediately after installation.

tasks.title: Update System Packages
tasks.objective: Refresh the local package index to ensure the latest Nginx packages and dependencies are available.
tasks.rationale: Updating before installation ensures compatibility with Ubuntu 24.04 repositories and avoids installing outdated components.

tasks.title: Install Nginx Package
tasks.objective: Download and install the Nginx web server and its core dependencies.
tasks.rationale: This installs the main Nginx binary, configuration files, and default SSL certificates provided by Ubuntu.
tasks.expected_output: Nginx installation log showing package completion.
success_criteria: Dependencies like pcre2 and zlib are resolved.

tasks.title: Start Nginx Service
tasks.objective: Activate the Nginx service and ensure it starts successfully.
tasks.rationale: Nginx does not start automatically just by installation on Ubuntu; the systemd service must be enabled and started.
success_criteria: Service state is 'active' for both 'started' and 'enabled'.
No logs indicate immediate start failure.

tasks.title: Check Service Status
tasks.objective: Verify the health and status of the Nginx daemon.
tasks.rationale: Confirming the service is healthy before moving to configuration or testing ensures stability.
tasks.expected_output: Full status output showing 'Active: active (running)' and load time.

tasks.title: Test HTTP Connectivity
tasks.objective: Validate that the web server responds correctly to client requests.
tasks.rationale: This confirms the Nginx instance is listening on port 80 and serving content as expected.
tasks.expected_output: HTTP headers indicating a valid response (e.g., '200 OK').
success_criteria: Server header identifies 'nginx' or the default welcome page content is returned.

tasks.title: Review Default Configuration
tasks.objective: Inspect the default Nginx configuration file for correctness.
tasks.rationale: Ubuntu 24.04 provides a specific default config; understanding its location (sites-enabled/default) helps prevent conflicts later.
tasks.expected_output: Contents of the default site configuration and list of enabled sites.
success_criteria: Configuration syntax does not show obvious errors in headers.

tasks.title: Run Configuration Syntax Check
tasks.objective: Validate the Nginx configuration files for syntax errors.
tasks.rationale: Preventing future restart failures by ensuring the config is valid before relying on it during operation.
tasks.expected_output: Message indicating 'nginx: configuration file /etc/nginx/nginx.conf test is successful'.
success_criteria: Output states the test is 'successful' (exit code 0).
No warnings regarding missing upstreams or SSL paths.

tasks.title: Configure Firewall Rules (UFW)
tasks.objective: Allow HTTP and HTTPS traffic through the host firewall.
tasks.rationale: Ubuntu 24.04 uses UFW; without explicit rules, incoming port 80/443 connections will be blocked by default.
tasks.expected_output: Confirmation messages showing rules added (e.g., 'Allow OpenSSH' is already enabled, 'Allow HTTP', 'Allow HTTPS').
success_criteria: UFW status lists port 80 and 443 as ALLOW.

tasks.title: Final Verification via External IP
tasks.objective: Confirm the server is accessible from an external perspective using its public IP.
tasks.rationale: Internal checks pass, but external DNS resolution or firewall misconfigurations might still block access; this validates end-to-end connectivity.
tasks.expected_output: Successful HTTP response received from the public IP address.
success_criteria: Response code is 200 when querying the external IP.

tasks.title: Document Installation Details
tasks.objective: Record key details about the installation for future reference.
tasks.rationale: Maintaining an audit trail of installed versions, ports, and configuration files aids in troubleshooting or compliance checks.
tasks.expected_output: A summary containing the Nginx version string and current active firewall rules.
